title: Apache Syncope Flaws Enable SQL Injection, JWT Token Takeover and Code Injection
content_md: Apache Syncope has disclosed three important vulnerabilities that could allow privileged administrators to execute arbitrary SQL commands, bypass Groovy sandbox protections to inject code, and hijack higher-privileged user sessions through exposed JWT access tokens. Tracked as CVE-2026-82232, CVE-2026-77147, and CVE-2026-73178, the flaws affect multiple Apache Syncope 3.0, 4.0, and 4.1 releases. Organizations using affected instances of the identity-management platform should prioritize upgrades to Syncope 4.0.8 or 4.1.3, which address all three vulnerabilities. Apache Syncope Flaws CVE-2026-82232 is an SQL injection vulnerability in Apache Syncope’s syncope-core-persistence-jpa component. The issue results from improper neutralization of SQL special characters within sort clauses supplied during Task search operations. An administrator holding adequate entitlements can exploit the unsanitized sort parameter to execute arbitrary SQL via stacked queries. In this type of attack, an attacker appends additional SQL commands to a legitimate query, potentially allowing them to read, alter, or delete database records depending on the permissions assigned to the application’s database account. The vulnerability affects Apache Syncope versions 3.0.0-M0 through 3.0.16, versions 4.0.0-M0 through 4.0.7, and versions 4.1.0-M0 through 4.1.2. Security researcher Alon Galili was credited with reporting the flaw. CVE-2026-77147 affects the syncope-core-spring component and has been classified
